expected_miss.reason: challenge 15: forge valid JWT tokens. Mechanism in source: algorithm confusion (RSA public key re-used as the HS256 secret) — NOT a wordlist-weak secret. 3A's wordlist check targets a different mechanism; an engine hit is a confirmed positive, a miss is an honest NOT-FOUND, not a false negative.
challenges 4+5: endpoints leaking sensitive data of other users and an internal video property.

challenge 15: forge valid JWT tokens. crAPI issues RS256 and serves the public key at /.well-known/jwks.json — the documented forgery is HS256 signed with that public key (the confusion differential fam1 runs verbatim).

challenge 15 ('find ANY one way to forge'): run 9 live-proved the dashboard reads the token's sub claim without signature verification, so the alg=none differential shares the documented mechanism's root cause (CWE-347).

challenge 8 names a 'shadow API endpoint' (undocumented surface); the spec supplied is main's crapi-openapi-spec.json against the pinned v1.1.5 deployment — a hit is judged against the documented spec/deployment version drift (the spec does not exist at the v1.1.5 tag).

spec-declared-but-dead (spec drift) and deprecated-but-alive are the OWASP API8:2023 'outdated API versions' class; the supplied spec is main's against the pinned v1.1.5 deployment — the version drift is the documented context.

the declared candidate POST /workshop/api/mechanic/signup (on the official spec) has the classic check-then-insert handler in the pinned v1.1.5 source (filter(email).exists() then User.objects.create) with a UNIQUE email constraint — the single-winner invariant. The burst email is unique per run; >1 winner is a confirmed positive, 1 winner an honest TESTED_NEGATIVE (constraint held).
